newsitem.title: USA: G7 to send Japanese, French envoys to Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: G7 to send Japanese, French envoys to Cambodia.

text.p: Leaders of the Group of Seven leading industrial countries and Russia agreed on Friday night to send French and Japanese envoys to Cambodia to study the situation there, officials said.

A Japanese official source said they approved a Japanese proposal to send the envoys during a working dinner at the start of the annual G7 summit here, in which Russian President Boris Yeltsin is also participating.
The two envoys, representing the summit countries, might go to Phnom Penh next week, ahead of a scheduled visit there by U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, the source said.

If Albright went ahead with her trip, they might report their views on the situation in Cambodia to Albright on the spot, the source added. U.S. officials have said there are concerns over Albright's security in Cambodia.
The source said the Japanese envoy would be Yukio Imagawa, a former ambassador to Cambodia, and France was still considering who to send.

The summit took its decision soon after the Cambodian government announced the capture of Khmer Rouge strongman Pol Pot, blamed for mass killings when the hardline communist guerrilla movement ruled the country from 1975 to 1979.
Efforts would be made to try him before an international tribunal, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh said.
